nodes.name: Halloysite Template to NCNTs
nodes.procedure: Natural halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) were used as templates (Figure 1b), and surface-polymerized polydopamine was used as a bridge to construct electrically rich NCNTs, including good conductivity, abundant surface exposure, and curvature surface electric field concentration (Figure S1, Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: Natural halloysite nanotubes (HNTs) were used as templates... construct electrically rich NCNTs, including good conductivity, abundant surface exposure, and curvature surface electric field concentration (Figure S1)

nodes.name: Borane Cluster Loading
nodes.procedure: The boron clusters reducing agent was introduced onto NCNTs by in situ crystallization using NCNTs as the carrier, which endowed NCNTs with reducing ability.
nodes.source_text: the boron clusters reducing agent was introduced onto NCNTs by in situ crystallization

nodes.name: PtRu Alloy Formation
nodes.procedure: Simultaneous in situ reduction and in situ loading of Pt⁴⁺ and Ru³⁺ were subsequently achieved using the reducing ability of (TBA)₂[B₁₂H₁₂]/NCNTs under heating conditions. Highly dispersed, ultrasmall particle size PtRu alloy was finally constructed on NCNTs.

unit_operations.name: In situ Reduction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: in situ reduction of noble metal ions, such as Pt⁴⁺, Ru³⁺, or Pt⁴⁺/Ru³⁺

nodes.source_text: achieving simultaneous in situ reduction and in situ loading of Pt⁴⁺ and Ru³⁺ were subsequently achieved

nodes.name: Pt/NCNTs Preparation
nodes.procedure: Pt/NCNTs was prepared using the same boron cluster in situ reduction method but using only Pt⁴⁺ precursor.
nodes.source_text: crystallization of boron clusters onto the surface of NCNTs was successfully achieved by in situ conversion of Pt⁴⁺

nodes.name: Ru/NCNTs Preparation
nodes.procedure: Ru/NCNTs was prepared using the same boron cluster in situ reduction method but using only Ru³⁺ precursor.
nodes.source_text: crystallization of boron clusters onto the surface of NCNTs was successfully achieved by in situ conversion of Ru³⁺

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR confirms boron clusters on NCNTs support of PtRu/NCNTs with B-H stretching at 2476 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy confirmed the successful crystallization of boron clusters onto the surface of NCNTs, with characteristic signals of both NCNTs and [B₁₂H₁₂]²⁻ appearing in (TBA)₂[B₁₂H₁₂]/NCNTs, with signals near 2476 cm⁻¹ attributed to the B-H stretching vibration.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows Pt(111), Pt(200), Pt(220), Pt(311), Pt(222) peaks at 39.76°, 46.24°, 67.45°, 81.29°, 85.71° and Ru(100), Ru(002), Ru(101), Ru(102), Ru(110), Ru(103), Ru(200), Ru(112) peaks confirming formation of PtRu alloy in PtRu/NCNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) signals ... simultaneous Pt and Ru signals were observed in PtRu/NCNTs, suggesting that the boron clusters precrystallized onto the surface of NCNTs achieved simultaneous in situ reduction of Pt⁴⁺ and Ru³⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows PtRu/NCNTs mainly exist as zero-valent Pt and Ru⁰ with Pt in electron-rich state and Ru in electron-deficient state due to electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) signals show that PtRu/NCNTs and Pt/NCNTs mainly exist in the form of zero-valent Pt ... The significant change in binding energy in the XPS signal indicates that after the formation of PtRu/NCNTs, Pt enters an electron rich state, while Ru enters an electron-deficient state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt-L edge EXAFS shows distinct Pt-Pt and Pt-Ru signals; Ru-K edge shows Ru-Ru and Ru-Pt signals confirming PtRu alloy formation with strong Pt-Ru interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of PtRu alloys is evidenced by the distinct emergence of new signals observable in the Xray fine structure (EXAFS). Distinct Pt-Pt and Pt-Ru signals were observed in the Pt-L EXAFS of PtRu/NCNTs ... pronounced Ru-Ru and Ru-Pt signals were detected in the Ru-K edge EXAFS of PtRu/NCNTs.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows PtRu/NCNTs, Pt/NCNTs, Ru/NCNTs maintain hollow tubular morphology similar to NCNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) imaging showed that (TBA)₂[B₁₂H₁₂]/NCNTs, PtRu/NCNTs, Pt/NCNTs, and Ru/NCNTs all exhibited a hollow tubular morphology, which was similar to the morphology of NCNTs.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption/desorption isotherms show type IV curves with pore sizes 2.5-50 nm and specific surface area of 110.5 m²/g for mesoporous PtRu/NCNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ adsorption/desorption isotherms of PtRu/NCNTs in the specific surface and pore size analysis tests (BET) were type IV curves, with most of the pore sizes ranging from 2.5 to 50 nm ... PtRu/NCNTs exist in mesoporous form with a large specific surface area (110.5 m² g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-STEM shows ultrasmall PtRu particles with lattice fringes of 0.231 nm (Ru(100)) and 0.223 nm (Pt(111)) confirming alloy formation; average particle size 1.64 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) images clearly showed that large-size nanoparticle aggregation was almost invisible in PtRu/NCNTs ... the spacing of 0.231 nm (green dashed line) and 0.223 nm (orange dashed line) streaks are respectively attributed to the lattice fringes of the Ru(100) crystallographic plane and Pt(111) crystallographic plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Pt, Ru, B, C, N elements in PtRu/NCNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: through elemental mappings and energy dispersive spectroscopy, it can be clearly seen that the elements Pt, Ru, B, C, and N are present in the PtRu/NCNTs and show a uniform distribution.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-FTIR shows increasing H₂O adsorption at 1500-1700 and 3200-3500 cm⁻¹, and Pt-H/Ru-H bonds at 1900-2200 cm⁻¹ during HER on PtRu/NCNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ATR-FTIRA signals showed a continuous increase in the signal intensity at 1500-1700 and 3200-3500 cm⁻¹ in PtRu/NCNTs with increasing reduction potential ... the presence of Pt-H and Ru-H bonds could be observed in the region of 1900-2200 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping confirms presence of B element in (TBA)₂[B₁₂H₁₂]/NCNTs support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the presence of elemental B was observed in the elemental mapping images of (TBA)₂[B₁₂H₁₂]/NCNTs.
